candidates.title: Nebuchadnezzar's campaign against Jerusalem in Jehoiakim's third year; temple vessels taken to Shinar
candidates.description: In the third year of Jehoiakim, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it; Jehoiakim was given into his hand with some temple vessels, which were carried to the land of Shinar and put in the treasure house of his god.

temporal_statements.phrase: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah

ambiguities: "Third year" vs Jeremiah's "fourth year" (Jer 25:1; 46:2): regnal-reckoning question.
No Babylonian source names Jerusalem before 597.

candidates.title: Selection, renaming and training of young Judean nobles for the Babylonian court
candidates.description: The king ordered Ashpenaz to bring in royal and noble Israelite youths to be taught the learning and language of the Chaldeans for three years with provisions from the king's table; Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah received Babylonian names.

temporal_statements.phrase: nourished three years

ambiguities: Whether "eunuchs" (sārîs) denotes castration or court officials generally.

candidates.title: Daniel's refusal of the king's food and the ten-day test
candidates.description: Daniel resolved not to defile himself with the king's food and wine; the steward tested the four on vegetables and water for ten days, after which they looked healthier, and their rations were changed.

temporal_statements.phrase: ten days

ambiguities: The narrative states divine favour (1:9); not testable historically.

candidates.title: The youths' wisdom and their presentation before Nebuchadnezzar
candidates.description: God gave the four knowledge and wisdom, Daniel understanding of visions and dreams; at the end of the appointed time they were presented to the king, who found them ten times better than his magicians and enchanters.

temporal_statements.phrase: At the end of the days which the king had appointed

ambiguities: Relation of the three-year training to "the second year of Nebuchadnezzar" in Dan 2:1.

candidates.title: Daniel continued until the first year of King Cyrus
candidates.description: A closing note that Daniel continued until the first year of Cyrus.

temporal_statements.phrase: even to the first year of King Cyrus

ambiguities: "Continued" (at court? in life?) — Dan 10:1 dates a later vision to Cyrus's third year. To be researched with Dan 5–6 (fall of Babylon, Cyrus).

verse_coverage.notes: Language switch: the narrative continues in Aramaic from the second half of this verse to 7:28.

candidates.title: Nebuchadnezzar's troubling dream and the decree against the wise men
candidates.description: In his second year Nebuchadnezzar demanded that his diviners tell him both his dream and its meaning; when they could not, he decreed the death of Babylon's wise men, including Daniel and his companions, whom Arioch went to execute.

temporal_statements.phrase: In the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar

ambiguities: "Second year" vs the three-year training (1:5, 18).
The text switches from Hebrew to Aramaic at 2:4b ("in the Syrian language") and stays in Aramaic to 7:28.

candidates.title: The secret revealed to Daniel and his interpretation before the king
candidates.description: Daniel and his companions prayed; the secret was revealed to Daniel in a night vision; Arioch brought him to the king, and Daniel attributed the revelation to the God of heaven.

candidates.title: The statue of four metals and the stone (dream content)
candidates.description: The dream image as recounted by Daniel.
ambiguities: Symbolic content — not a historical occurrence.

candidates.title: The four kingdoms and the everlasting kingdom (interpretation)
candidates.description: Daniel's interpretation of the image as a sequence of kingdoms followed by God's everlasting kingdom.

temporal_statements.phrase: In the days of those kings

ambiguities: Only the head of gold is identified in the text.

candidates.title: Nebuchadnezzar honours Daniel and appoints him over the province of Babylon
candidates.description: The king prostrated himself, confessed Daniel's God, made Daniel ruler over the province of Babylon and chief over the wise men, and appointed his three companions over the province's affairs.

verse_coverage.notes: Greek Daniel inserts the Prayer of Azariah and the Song of the Three Young Men after this verse (non-canonical; indexed as a document).
The Aramaic text continues with 3:31–33, which English Bibles number 4:1–3.

candidates.title: The golden image and its dedication on the plain of Dura
candidates.description: Nebuchadnezzar set up a gold image 60 by 6 cubits on the plain of Dura and summoned the officials of the provinces to its dedication; at the sound of the instruments all peoples were to fall down and worship, on pain of the furnace.
ambiguities: No date in the Aramaic text; Brenton's Septuagint reads "in his eighteenth year".
Instrument names include Greek loanwords.

candidates.title: Accusation of the three Jews and their refusal
candidates.description: Chaldeans accused Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego of not serving the king's gods; summoned, they refused to worship the image, trusting their God to deliver them or not.

temporal_statements.phrase: at that time

ambiguities: Daniel is absent from the chapter.

candidates.title: The fiery furnace and the deliverance
candidates.description: The furnace was heated seven times hotter; the bound men were thrown in, the executioners died, the king saw four men walking unharmed in the fire, and the three came out without even the smell of fire.
ambiguities: Identity of the fourth figure (3:25; the king calls him an angel in 3:28). English versions differ: "a son of the gods" vs "the Son of God".
Greek Daniel inserts the Prayer of Azariah and the Song of the Three after 3:23 (non-canonical; SPEC 5.6).

candidates.title: Nebuchadnezzar's decree and the promotion of the three
candidates.description: The king blessed their God, decreed death for anyone speaking against him, and promoted the three in the province of Babylon.

candidates.title: Nebuchadnezzar's proclamation to all peoples (letter frame)
candidates.description: The chapter is framed as a royal letter in which the king praises the Most High.
ambiguities: In the Aramaic text these verses are 3:31–33.

candidates.title: The king's dream of the tree; Daniel summoned to interpret
candidates.description: At rest in his palace, the king dreamed and summoned his diviners, who failed; Daniel/Belteshazzar was called.

candidates.title: The great tree and the watcher's decree (dream content)
candidates.description: The dream image as recounted by the king.

temporal_statements.phrase: let seven times pass over him

ambiguities: Symbolic content.

candidates.title: Daniel's interpretation: the decree against the king
candidates.description: Daniel identifies the tree as the king and announces his humbling for seven times, urging repentance.

candidates.title: The boast over Babylon and the king's madness
candidates.description: Twelve months later the king boasted over the Babylon he had built; a voice from heaven announced the sentence and he was driven from men, living like an animal.

temporal_statements.phrase: At the end of twelve months

ambiguities: Proposed Nabonidus tradition behind the story.

candidates.title: Restoration and confession
candidates.description: At the end of the days the king's reason returned; he praised the Most High and was restored to his kingdom with added greatness.

temporal_statements.phrase: At the end of the days

candidates.title: Belshazzar's feast with the Jerusalem temple vessels
candidates.description: Belshazzar holds a feast for a thousand lords and drinks from the gold and silver vessels taken from the Jerusalem temple, praising idols.
ambiguities: "Father" (5:2, 11, 13, 18) for Nebuchadnezzar, whereas Babylonian texts make Belshazzar the son of Nabonidus.

candidates.title: The writing on the wall; the wise men fail; the queen recommends Daniel
candidates.description: A hand writes on the plaster wall; the king offers purple, a gold chain and the rank of "third ruler" to any who can read it; the queen recalls Daniel from Nebuchadnezzar's days.

temporal_statements.phrase: In the same hour

ambiguities: Identity of "the queen" (queen mother or wife) is not stated.
"Third ruler" — meaning debated.

candidates.title: Daniel's rebuke recalling Nebuchadnezzar's humbling
candidates.description: Daniel declines the gifts and reminds the king how Nebuchadnezzar was humbled until he acknowledged the Most High.

candidates.title: The inscription MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN and its interpretation
candidates.description: Daniel reads the words as numbered, weighed and divided: the kingdom is ended and given to the Medes and Persians.
ambiguities: 5:25 "upharsin" vs 5:28 "peres"; some ancient versions have a single mene (Seow, via Wikipedia).

candidates.title: Daniel honoured as third ruler
candidates.description: Belshazzar clothes Daniel in purple, gives him a gold chain and proclaims him third ruler.

candidates.title: Belshazzar slain that night
candidates.description: That night Belshazzar the Chaldean king was killed.

temporal_statements.phrase: In that night

ambiguities: Daniel does not say who killed him or name Cyrus here.

candidates.title: Darius the Mede receives the kingdom, aged about 62
candidates.description: Darius the Mede received the kingdom, being about sixty-two years old.
ambiguities: Identity of Darius the Mede.
Aramaic numbering: English 5:31 = Aramaic 6:1.

candidates.title: The fall of Babylon to the Medes and Persians (implied)
candidates.description: The interpretation (5:28) and the closing verses imply the transfer of Babylon to the Medes and Persians, which Babylonian sources date to Tašrītu of Nabonidus's 17th year.
ambiguities: Daniel does not narrate the capture itself.

candidates.title: Darius sets 120 satraps and three chief officials over the kingdom; Daniel distinguished
candidates.description: Darius appoints 120 satraps under three chief officials, of whom Daniel is one; the king plans to set Daniel over the whole realm.
ambiguities: English 6:1 = Aramaic 6:2.
Scope of "the kingdom" (Babylonia or the empire) and of the term satrap.

candidates.title: The officials' plot and the thirty-day decree
candidates.description: Unable to fault Daniel, the officials persuade Darius to sign an irrevocable 30-day decree forbidding petitions to any god or man except the king.

temporal_statements.phrase: for thirty days

ambiguities: "The law of the Medes and Persians, which doesn't alter" (6:8).

candidates.title: Daniel prays toward Jerusalem and is accused
candidates.description: Daniel continues to pray three times a day at open windows toward Jerusalem; the officials accuse him and hold the king to the unalterable decree.

temporal_statements.phrase: until the going down of the sun

candidates.title: Daniel in the lions' den and his deliverance
candidates.description: Daniel is cast into the den, sealed with the king's signet; the king fasts overnight and at dawn finds him unharmed, his God having sent an angel to shut the lions' mouths.

temporal_statements.phrase: very early in the morning

candidates.title: The accusers and their families thrown to the lions
candidates.description: The king has the accusers, their children and wives cast into the den, where the lions overpower them.

candidates.title: Darius's decree to all peoples to fear the God of Daniel
candidates.description: Darius writes to all peoples ordering reverence for the living God whose kingdom will not be destroyed.

candidates.title: Summary: Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius and the reign of Cyrus
candidates.description: A closing notice that Daniel prospered under Darius and under Cyrus the Persian.
ambiguities: Read as successive reigns or appositionally ("the reign of Darius, that is, the reign of Cyrus").

verse_coverage.notes: Last verse of the Aramaic section.

candidates.title: Daniel's dream-vision in the first year of Belshazzar, written down
candidates.description: Daniel has a dream and visions on his bed and writes down the sum of the matter.

temporal_statements.phrase: In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon

ambiguities: Belshazzar never had regnal years in Babylonian dating; the counting basis of "first year" is unknown.

candidates.title: Four beasts from the great sea
candidates.description: The four winds stir the great sea; a winged lion, a bear with three ribs, a four-headed winged leopard and a terrible fourth beast with iron teeth and ten horns come up.
ambiguities: Symbolic content; identifications beyond the text are interpretive.

candidates.title: The little horn with eyes and a boasting mouth
candidates.description: A little horn rises among the ten, uprooting three, with human eyes and a mouth speaking arrogantly.

candidates.title: The Ancient of Days and the heavenly court; the beast destroyed
candidates.description: Thrones are set; the Ancient of Days sits; the court sits and books are opened; the beast is slain and burned; the other beasts lose dominion but live for a time.

temporal_statements.phrase: for a season and a time

ambiguities: Plural thrones but one who sits (cf. b. Sanh 38b).

candidates.title: One like a son of man comes with the clouds and receives everlasting dominion
candidates.description: A human-like figure comes with the clouds of heaven to the Ancient of Days and is given an everlasting kingdom.
ambiguities: Identity of the figure (individual, collective, angelic).

candidates.title: Daniel troubled; asks a bystander for the meaning
candidates.description: Daniel is troubled and asks one of those standing by, who explains.
ambiguities: The interpreter is unnamed (cf. Gabriel in 8:16).

candidates.title: The interpretation: four kings; the saints receive the kingdom
candidates.description: The four beasts are four kings who will arise; the saints of the Most High will receive the kingdom forever.
ambiguities: "Kings" (7:17) and "kingdom" (7:23) are used of the same beasts.

candidates.title: The fourth beast, ten horns and little horn explained
candidates.description: The fourth beast is a fourth kingdom; ten kings arise from it and another who subdues three, speaks against the Most High, wears out the saints and seeks to change times and law for a time, times and half a time; judgment sits and the kingdom is given to the people of the saints.

temporal_statements.phrase: until a time and times and half a time

ambiguities: "Saints/holy ones of the Most High": humans or angels.

candidates.title: Daniel keeps the matter in his heart
candidates.description: The end of the account; Daniel is troubled and keeps the matter to himself.
ambiguities: End of the Aramaic section of Daniel (2:4b–7:28).

candidates.title: A second vision in Belshazzar's third year, at Susa by the Ulai
candidates.description: Daniel sees a vision in the third year of Belshazzar, finding himself (in the vision) in the citadel of Susa by the river Ulai.

temporal_statements.phrase: In the third year of the reign of King Belshazzar

ambiguities: Whether Daniel was physically at Susa or only saw himself there "in the vision" (8:2).
Return to Hebrew from 8:1.

candidates.title: The ram with two horns
candidates.description: A ram with two high horns, the higher coming up last, pushes west, north and south.

candidates.title: The goat from the west; the great horn broken; four horns
candidates.description: A goat with a notable horn races from the west without touching the ground, breaks the ram's horns; at its height the great horn is broken and four horns rise toward the four winds.

candidates.title: The little horn against the host, the prince and the sanctuary
candidates.description: A little horn grows toward the south, east and the glorious land, casts down some of the host and stars, magnifies itself against the prince of the host, removes the continual offering and casts down the sanctuary.
ambiguities: "The prince of the host" (8:11) and "prince of princes" (8:25): God or the high priest.

candidates.title: Holy ones ask "how long?": 2,300 evenings and mornings
candidates.description: One holy one asks how long the desolation will last; the answer is 2,300 evenings and mornings, after which the sanctuary will be cleansed.

temporal_statements.phrase: To two thousand and three hundred evenings and mornings

ambiguities: 2,300 days or 1,150 days (2,300 offerings).
"Unto me" (MT) vs "unto him" (versions; Driver).

candidates.title: Gabriel commanded to explain; Daniel falls into a deep sleep
candidates.description: A voice from between the banks of the Ulai commands Gabriel to explain; the vision concerns "the time of the end".

temporal_statements.phrase: the vision belongs to the time of the end

ambiguities: First naming of an angel in the Bible (Gabriel).

candidates.title: The ram is the kings of Media and Persia; the goat the king of Greece
candidates.description: Gabriel identifies the ram with the kings of Media and Persia, the goat with the king of Greece, the great horn with the first king, and the four horns with four kingdoms that arise from his nation.
ambiguities: The first king and the four kingdoms are not named.

candidates.title: The king of fierce face
candidates.description: In the latter time of their kingdom a fierce, cunning king will arise, destroy the holy people, stand against the prince of princes and be broken "without human hands".

temporal_statements.phrase: In the latter time of their kingdom

candidates.title: The vision is true; seal it up for many days
candidates.description: The vision of the evenings and mornings is true but belongs to many days to come.

temporal_statements.phrase: it belongs to many days to come

candidates.title: Daniel faints, is sick, then does the king's business
candidates.description: Daniel is ill for some days, then returns to the king's business, astonished and without understanding.

temporal_statements.phrase: was sick for some days

ambiguities: "The king's business" is read by some as implying Daniel was at Susa in person.

candidates.title: The first year of Darius son of Ahasuerus, the Mede
candidates.description: The prayer is dated to the first year of Darius, son of Ahasuerus, a Mede, who was made king over the realm of the Chaldeans.

temporal_statements.phrase: In the first year of Darius the son of Ahasuerus

ambiguities: "Son of Ahasuerus" adds a patronymic not known from external sources; Darius's identity is disputed (see Dan 5–6 records).
"Was made king" (passive) is read by some as appointment by Cyrus.

candidates.title: Daniel understands Jeremiah's seventy years from "the books"
candidates.description: Daniel understands from the books the number of years for the desolations of Jerusalem: seventy years (Jer 25:11–12; 29:10).

temporal_statements.phrase: even seventy years

ambiguities: Which events begin and end the seventy years.
"The books" — evidence of a collection of prophetic writings (Driver).

candidates.title: Daniel's prayer of confession and supplication
candidates.description: With fasting, sackcloth and ashes Daniel confesses Israel's sin and the justice of the curse of the law of Moses, and asks God to turn his anger from Jerusalem and the desolate sanctuary for his own name's sake.
ambiguities: Deuteronomic language; the prayer's relation to Neh 9 and Baruch 1–2 is discussed by commentators (not researched here).

candidates.title: Gabriel arrives about the time of the evening offering
candidates.description: While Daniel is still praying, Gabriel, whom he had seen in the earlier vision, comes in swift flight about the time of the evening offering to give him understanding.

temporal_statements.phrase: about the time of the evening offering

ambiguities: "Evening offering" names a time of day while no Temple offering was being made.

candidates.title: Seventy weeks are decreed on your people and your holy city
candidates.description: Seventy weeks are decreed to finish transgression, end sins, atone for iniquity, bring in everlasting righteousness, seal vision and prophet, and anoint a most holy (place or one).

temporal_statements.phrase: Seventy weeks are decreed

ambiguities: "Weeks" (heptads) of years is the usual reading but is not stated.
"Anoint the most holy": a place (altar/sanctuary) or a person.

candidates.title: From the going out of the word to an anointed one, a prince: seven weeks and sixty-two weeks
candidates.description: From the going out of a word to restore and build Jerusalem to an anointed one, a prince, seven weeks; for sixty-two weeks it will be built with street and moat in troubled times.

temporal_statements.phrase: seven weeks and sixty-two weeks

ambiguities: Punctuation: the Masoretic accent divides "seven weeks" from "sixty-two weeks" (RV, WEB-like); the AV joins them (69 weeks to the Messiah) — Driver.
Which "word" or decree starts the count.
Whether "an anointed one, a prince" is Cyrus, Jeshua, or the Messiah.

candidates.title: An anointed one cut off; the people of a coming prince destroy city and sanctuary
candidates.description: After the sixty-two weeks an anointed one is cut off and has nothing; the people of a prince who comes destroy the city and sanctuary; desolations are decreed until the end of the war.

temporal_statements.phrase: After the sixty-two weeks

ambiguities: Is this "anointed one" the same as in 9:25?
"And will have nothing" — an unexplained crux (Montgomery); AV "but not for himself" is rejected by Driver.
2 Maccabees 4:33–35 (Onias III) is outside the 66-book index; linked through the Onias III record instead.

candidates.title: A firm covenant for one week; sacrifice ceases in the middle; the abomination that desolates
candidates.description: He makes a firm covenant with many for one week; in the middle of the week he makes sacrifice and offering cease; on the wing of abominations comes one who makes desolate until the decreed end.

temporal_statements.phrase: for one week. In the middle of the week

ambiguities: Subject of "he will make a firm covenant": the coming prince, the Messiah, or Antiochus.

candidates.title: Amos's prophetic words dated by the superscription
candidates.description: The superscription attributes the book to Amos, one of the herdsmen of Tekoa, and dates what he "saw" concerning Israel to the days of Uzziah of Judah and Jeroboam son of Joash of Israel.

temporal_statements.phrase: in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash

ambiguities: Whether the dating refers to a single vision occasion or a longer ministry.
Whether Uzziah's 'days' include his coregency years (model-dependent).

candidates.title: The earthquake in the days of Uzziah
candidates.description: The superscription places Amos's words "two years before the earthquake", referring to a known earthquake without further description.

temporal_statements.phrase: two years before the earthquake

ambiguities: Whether Zechariah 14:5 refers to the same earthquake (likely by wording; tested in Rule 04).
Whether "two years" is exact or counted inclusively.

candidates.title: The LORD roars from Zion
candidates.description: Poetic announcement that the LORD will roar from Zion, with pastures mourning and the top of Carmel withering.
ambiguities: Some interpreters connect the imagery to drought or to the earthquake; no such link is stated in the text.

candidates.title: Oracle against Damascus
candidates.description: Judgment oracle against Damascus: fire on the house of Hazael and the palaces of Ben Hadad; the people of Aram to go into captivity to Kir.
ambiguities: 2 Kings 16:9 records Tiglath-pileser deporting Damascus to Kir — a proposed fulfillment to evaluate in Rule 04.

candidates.title: Damascus "threshed Gilead"
candidates.description: The oracle cites Aramean (Damascus) aggression against Gilead as the grounds for judgment.
ambiguities: Likely refers to Aramean campaigns of Hazael's era (cf. 2 Kgs 10:32–33); identification to be researched.

candidates.title: Oracle against Gaza and the Philistines
candidates.description: Judgment oracle against Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon and Ekron.

candidates.title: Gaza deported whole communities to Edom
candidates.description: The oracle cites Gaza carrying away whole communities to hand them over to Edom.
ambiguities: Specific occasion unidentified.

candidates.title: Oracle against Tyre
candidates.description: Judgment oracle against Tyre.

candidates.title: Tyre delivered communities to Edom, breaking a "brotherly covenant"
candidates.description: The oracle cites Tyre delivering whole communities to Edom and not remembering a brotherly covenant.
ambiguities: The covenant referred to is not identified in the text.

candidates.title: Oracle against Edom
candidates.description: Judgment oracle against Edom: fire on Teman and the palaces of Bozrah.

candidates.title: Edom pursued "his brother" with the sword
candidates.description: The oracle cites Edom pursuing his brother with the sword and unending anger.
ambiguities: "His brother" is commonly read as Israel/Judah; the specific conflict is unidentified.

candidates.title: Oracle against Ammon
candidates.description: Judgment oracle against Ammon: fire on the wall of Rabbah; its king and princes to go into captivity.

candidates.title: Ammon's atrocities in Gilead to enlarge its border
candidates.description: The oracle cites Ammonite atrocities against pregnant women of Gilead in order to enlarge their border.
ambiguities: Specific campaign unidentified.
